BLAKE3.description: Calculates BLAKE3 hash string and returns the resulting set of bytes as FixedString. This cryptographic hash-function is integrated into ClickHouse with BLAKE3 Rust library. The function is rather fast and shows approximately two times faster performance compared to SHA-2, while generating hashes of the same length as SHA-256. It returns a BLAKE3 hash as a byte array with type FixedString(32).

args.name: message
args.description: The input string to hash. `String`

BLAKE3.returns: Returns the 32-byte BLAKE3 hash of the input string as a fixed-length string. `FixedString(32)`

IPv4CIDRToRange.description: Takes an IPv4 address with its Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) prefix length and returns the subnet's address range as a tuple of two IPv4 values: the first and last addresses in that subnet. For the IPv6 version see `IPv6CIDRToRange`.

args.name: ipv4
args.description: IPv4 address. `IPv4` or `String`

args.name: cidr
args.description: CIDR value. `UInt8`

IPv4CIDRToRange.returns: Returns a tuple with two IPv4 addresses representing the subnet range. `Tuple(IPv4, IPv4)`

IPv4NumToString.description: Converts a 32-bit integer to its IPv4 address string representation in dotted decimal notation (A.B.C.D format). Interprets the input using big-endian byte ordering.

args.name: num
args.description: IPv4 address as UInt32 number. `UInt32`

IPv4NumToString.returns: Returns a number representing the MAC address, or `0` if the format is invalid. `String`

IPv4NumToStringClassC.description: Converts a 32-bit integer to its IPv4 address string representation in dotted decimal notation (A.B.C.D format), similar to `IPv4NumToString` but using `xxx` instead of the last octet.

args.name: num
args.description: IPv4 address as UInt32 number. `UInt32`

IPv4NumToStringClassC.returns: Returns the IPv4 address string with xxx replacing the last octet. `String`
IPv4NumToStringClassC.example:
SELECT
    IPv4NumToStringClassC(ClientIP) AS k,
    count() AS c
FROM test.hits
GROUP BY k
ORDER BY c DESC
LIMIT 10

aes_encrypt_mysql.description: Encrypts text the same way as MySQL's `AES_ENCRYPT` function does. The resulting ciphertext can be decrypted with MySQL's `AES_DECRYPT` function. Produces the same ciphertext as the `encrypt` function for the same inputs. When `key` or `iv` are longer than they should normally be, `aes_encrypt_mysql` will stick to what MySQL's `aes_encrypt` does which is to 'fold' `key` and ignore the excess bi…

args.description: Encryption mode. `String`

args.name: plaintext
args.description: Text that should be encrypted. `String`

args.name: key
args.description: Encryption key. If the key is longer than required by `mode`, MySQL-specific key folding is performed. `String`

args.name: iv
args.description: Optional. Initialization vector. Only the first 16 bytes are taken into account. `String`

aes_encrypt_mysql.example:
-- Given equal input encrypt and aes_encrypt_mysql produce the same ciphertext:
SELECT encrypt('aes-256-ofb', 'Secret', '12345678910121314151617181920212', 'iviviviviviviviv') = aes_encrypt_mysql('aes-256-ofb', 'Secret', '12345678910121314151617181920212', 'iviviviviviviviv') AS ciphertexts_equal;

cramersV.description: Cramer's V (sometimes referred to as Cramer's phi) is a measure of association between two columns in a table. The result of the `cramersV` function ranges from 0 (corresponding to no association between the variables) to 1 and can reach 1 only when each value is completely determined by the other. It may be viewed as the association between two variables as a percentage of their maximum possib…

            number % 3 AS a,
            number % 5 AS b
        FROM
            numbers(150)
    );

FROM

            number % 10 AS a,
            number % 4 AS b
        FROM
            numbers(150)
    );

digits.description: Returns the digits of a number `n` which starts at the specified index `offset`. Counting starts from 1 with the following logic: - If `offset` is `0`, an exception is thrown, as `offset` is 1-based. - If `offset` is negative, counting starts `offset` digits from the end of the number, rather than from the beginning. - If `offset` is greater than the number of digits in `n`, `0` is returned.

args.name: n
args.description: The number to calculate digits from. `(U)Int8` or `(U)Int16` or `(U)Int32` or `(U)Int64`

args.name: offset
args.description: The starting position of the digit in `n`. `(U)Int8` or `(U)Int16` or `(U)Int32` or `(U)Int64`

args.name: length
args.description: Optional. The maximum length of the digits. `(U)Int8` or `(U)Int16` or `(U)Int32` or `(U)Int64`

digits.returns: The selected digits of `n`, interpreted as a `UInt64`. Returns `0` if the selected range is empty. Leading zeros are not preserved. `UInt64`

FROM

    number AS time,

    )

)

The first inner array contains all captures from group 1, the second from group 2, etc. If no matches are found, returns an empty array. `Array(Array(String))`

WITH '< Server: nginx
< Date: Tue, 22 Jan 2019 00:26:14 GMT
< Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
< Connection: keep-alive
' AS s
SELECT extractAllGroupsHorizontal(s, '< ([\\w\\-]+): ([^\\r\\n]+)');

extractAllGroupsVertical.description: Matches all groups of a string using a regular expression and returns an array of arrays, where each array includes matching fragments from every group, grouped in order of appearance in the input string.

args.name: regexp
args.description: Regular expression to match by. `const String` or `const FixedString`

Each match produces an array with elements corresponding to the capturing groups in the regular expression (group 1, group 2, etc.). If no matches are found, returns an empty array. `Array(Array(String))`
extractAllGroupsVertical.example:
WITH '< Server: nginx
< Date: Tue, 22 Jan 2019 00:26:14 GMT
< Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
< Connection: keep-alive
' AS s
SELECT extractAllGroupsVertical(s, '< ([\\w\\-]+): ([^\\r\\n]+)');

firstSignificantSubdomainCustom.description: Returns the first significant subdomain of a URL using a custom TLD (Top-Level Domain) list. The custom TLD list name refers to a configuration that defines which domain suffixes should be treated as top-level domains. This is useful for non-standard TLD hierarchies. The function uses a simplified URL parsing algorithm that assumes the protocol and everything following are stripped.

args.name: url
args.description: The URL to extract the subdomain from. `String`

args.name: tld_list_name
args.description: Name of the custom TLD list from the configuration. `String`

firstSignificantSubdomainCustomRFC.description: Similar to `firstSignificantSubdomainCustom` but uses RFC 3986 compliant URL parsing instead of the simplified algorithm.

args.name: url
args.description: The URL to extract the subdomain from. `String`

args.name: tld_list_name
args.description: Name of the custom TLD list from the configuration. `String`

firstSignificantSubdomainRFC.description: Returns the "first significant subdomain" according to RFC 1034.

flameGraph.description: Builds a flamegraph using the list of stacktraces. Outputs an array of strings which can be used by the flamegraph.pl utility to render an SVG of the flamegraph.

args.name: traces
args.description: A stacktrace, either as raw addresses or as already-symbolized strings (e.g. `arrayMap(addressToSymbol, trace)`). `Array(UInt64)` or `Array(String)`

args.name: size
args.description: Optional. An allocation size for memory profiling (default 1). `UInt64`

args.name: ptr
args.description: Optional. An allocation address (default 0). `UInt64`

flameGraph.returns: Returns an array of strings for use with flamegraph.pl utility. `Array(String)`
flameGraph.example:
SET query_profiler_cpu_time_period_ns=10000000;
SELECT SearchPhrase, COUNT(DISTINCT UserID) AS u FROM hits WHERE SearchPhrase <> '' GROUP BY SearchPhrase ORDER BY u DESC LIMIT 10;

flattenTuple.description: Flattens a named and nested tuple. The elements of the returned tuple are the paths of the input tuple.

args.name: input
args.description: Named and nested tuple to flatten. [`Tuple(n1 T1[, n2 T2, ... ])`](/sql-reference/data-types/tuple)

flattenTuple.returns: Returns an output tuple whose elements are paths from the original input. `Tuple(T)`

flipCoordinates.description: Flips the x and y coordinates of geometric objects. This operation swaps latitude and longitude, which is useful for converting between different coordinate systems or correcting coordinate order.

args.name: geometry
args.description: The geometry to transform. Supported types: Point (Tuple(Float64, Float64)), Ring (Array(Point)), Polygon (Array(Ring)), MultiPolygon (Array(Polygon)), LineString (Array(Point)), MultiLineString (Arra

flipCoordinates.returns: The geometry with flipped coordinates. The return type matches the input type. `Point` or `Ring` or `Polygon` or `MultiPolygon` or `LineString` or `MultiLineString` or `Geometry`

floor.description: Returns the largest rounded number less than or equal to `x`, where the rounded number is a multiple of `1 / 10 * N`, or the nearest number of the appropriate data type if `1 / 10 * N` isn't exact.

args.name: x
args.description: The value to round. `Float*` or `Decimal*` or `(U)Int*`

args.name: N
args.description: Optional. The number of decimal places to round to. Defaults to zero, which means rounding to an integer. Can be negative. `(U)Int*`

floor.returns: Returns a rounded number of the same type as `x`. `Float*` or `Decimal*` or `(U)Int*`

format.description: Format the `pattern` string with the values (strings, integers, etc.) listed in the arguments, similar to formatting in Python. The pattern string can contain replacement fields surrounded by curly braces `{}`. Anything not contained in braces is considered literal text and copied verbatim into the output. Literal brace character can be escaped by two braces: `{{` and `}}`. Field names can be n…

args.name: pattern
args.description: The format string containing placeholders. `String`

args.name: s0[, s1, ...]
args.description: One or more values to substitute into the pattern. `Any`

formatDateTime.description: Formats a date or date with time according to the given format string. `format` is a constant expression, so you cannot have multiple formats for a single result column.

args.name: datetime
args.description: A date or date time to format. `Date` or `Date32` or `DateTime` or `DateTime64`

args.name: format
args.description: Format string with replacement fields. `String`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Timezone name for the formatted time. `String`

formatDateTime.returns: Returns time and date values according to the determined format. `String`

formatDateTimeInJodaSyntax.description: Similar to `formatDateTime`, except that it formats datetime in Joda style instead of MySQL style. Refer to Joda Time documentation.

args.name: datetime
args.description: A date or date time to format. `DateTime` or `Date` or `Date32` or `DateTime64`

args.name: format
args.description: Format string with Joda-style replacement fields. `String`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Timezone name for the formatted time. `String`

formatDateTimeInJodaSyntax.returns: Returns time and date values according to the determined format. `String`

formatQuery.description: Returns a formatted, possibly multi-line, version of the given SQL query. Throws in case of a parsing error. [example:multiline]

args.name: query
args.description: The SQL query to be formatted. String

formatQuery.example: SELECT formatQuery('select a,    b FRom tab WHERE a > 3 and  b < 3');

formatQueryOrNull.description: Returns a formatted, possibly multi-line, version of the given SQL query. Returns NULL in case of a parsing error. [example:multiline]

args.name: query
args.description: The SQL query to be formatted. String

formatQueryOrNull.example: SELECT formatQuery('select a,    b FRom tab WHERE a > 3 and  b < 3');

formatQuerySingleLine.description: Like formatQuery() but the returned formatted string contains no line breaks. Throws in case of a parsing error. [example:multiline]

args.name: query
args.description: The SQL query to be formatted. String

formatQuerySingleLine.example: SELECT formatQuerySingleLine('select a,    b FRom tab WHERE a > 3 and  b < 3');

formatQuerySingleLineOrNull.description: Like formatQuery() but the returned formatted string contains no line breaks. Returns NULL in case of a parsing error. [example:multiline]

args.name: query
args.description: The SQL query to be formatted. `String`

formatQuerySingleLineOrNull.example: SELECT formatQuerySingleLine('select a,    b FRom tab WHERE a > 3 and  b < 3');

formatReadableDecimalSize.description: Given a size (number of bytes), this function returns a readable, rounded size with suffix (KB, MB, etc.) as a string.

args.name: value
args.description: Size in bytes. `Int8` or `Int16` or `Int32` or `Int64` or `UInt8` or `UInt16` or `UInt32` or `UInt64` or `Float32` or `Float64` or `Decimal`

args.name: precision
args.description: Optional. Number of digits after the decimal point. Defaults to 2. `const UInt8`

formatReadableDecimalSize.returns: Returns a readable, rounded size with suffix as a string. `String`
formatReadableDecimalSize.example:
SELECT
    arrayJoin([1, 1024, 1024*1024, 192851925]) AS filesize_bytes,
    formatReadableDecimalSize(filesize_bytes) AS filesize

formatReadableQuantity.description: Given a number, this function returns a rounded number with suffix (thousand, million, billion, etc.) as a string.

args.name: value
args.description: A number to format. `Int8` or `Int16` or `Int32` or `Int64` or `UInt8` or `UInt16` or `UInt32` or `UInt64` or `Float32` or `Float64` or `Decimal`

args.name: precision
args.description: Optional. Number of digits after the decimal point. Defaults to 2. `const UInt8`

formatReadableQuantity.returns: Returns a rounded number with suffix as a string. `String`
formatReadableQuantity.example:
SELECT
    arrayJoin([1024, 1234 * 1000, (4567 * 1000) * 1000, 98765432101234]) AS number,
    formatReadableQuantity(number) AS number_for_humans

formatReadableSize.description: Given a size (number of bytes), this function returns a readable, rounded size with suffix (KiB, MiB, etc.) as string.

args.name: value
args.description: Size in bytes. `Int8` or `Int16` or `Int32` or `Int64` or `UInt8` or `UInt16` or `UInt32` or `UInt64` or `Float32` or `Float64` or `Decimal`

args.name: precision
args.description: Optional. Number of digits after the decimal point. Defaults to 2. `const UInt8`

formatReadableSize.returns: Returns a readable, rounded size with suffix as a string. `String`
formatReadableSize.example:
SELECT
    arrayJoin([1, 1024, 1024*1024, 192851925]) AS filesize_bytes,
    formatReadableSize(filesize_bytes) AS filesize

formatReadableTimeDelta.description: Given a time interval (delta) in seconds or an `INTERVAL` expression, this function returns a time delta with year/month/day/hour/minute/second/millisecond/microsecond/nanosecond as a string.

args.name: column
args.description: A column with a numeric time delta, or an `INTERVAL` expression. Interval units of `MONTH` and greater are not supported. `Float64` or `Interval`

args.name: maximum_unit
args.description: Optional. Maximum unit to show. Acceptable values: `nanoseconds`, `microseconds`, `milliseconds`, `seconds`, `minutes`, `hours`, `days`, `months`, `years`. Default value: `years`. `const String`

args.name: minimum_unit
args.description: Optional. Minimum unit to show. All smaller units are truncated. Acceptable values: `nanoseconds`, `microseconds`, `milliseconds`, `seconds`, `minutes`, `hours`, `days`, `months`, `years`. If explicit

formatReadableTimeDelta.returns: Returns a time delta as a string. `String`
formatReadableTimeDelta.example:
SELECT
    arrayJoin([100, 12345, 432546534]) AS elapsed,
    formatReadableTimeDelta(elapsed) AS time_delta

formatRow.description: Converts arbitrary expressions into a string via given format.

args.name: format
args.description: Text format. For example, CSV, TSV. `String`

args.name: x, y, ...
args.description: Expressions. `Any`

formatRow.returns: A formatted string. (for text formats it's usually terminated with the new line character). `String`

formatRowNoNewline.description: Same as `formatRow`, but trims the newline character of each row.

args.name: format
args.description: Text format. For example, CSV, TSV. `String`

args.name: x, y, ...
args.description: Expressions. `Any`

formatRowNoNewline.returns: Returns a formatted string with newlines removed. `String`

fragment.description: Returns the fragment identifier without the initial hash symbol.

args.name: url
args.description: URL. `String`

fragment.returns: Returns the fragment identifier without the initial hash symbol. `String`

fromDaysSinceYearZero.description: For a given number of days elapsed since 1 January 0000, returns the corresponding date in the proleptic Gregorian calendar defined by ISO 8601.

args.name: days
args.description: The number of days passed since year zero. `UInt32`

fromDaysSinceYearZero.returns: Returns the date corresponding to the number of days passed since year zero. `Date`
fromDaysSinceYearZero.example:
SELECT
fromDaysSinceYearZero(739136) AS date1,
fromDaysSinceYearZero(toDaysSinceYearZero(toDate('2023-09-08'))) AS date2

fromDaysSinceYearZero32.description: For a given number of days elapsed since 1 January 0000, returns the corresponding date in the proleptic Gregorian calendar defined by ISO 8601. The calculation is the same as in MySQL's `FROM_DAYS()` function. The result is undefined if it cannot be represented within the bounds of the `Date32` type.

args.name: days
args.description: The number of days passed since year zero. `UInt32`

fromDaysSinceYearZero32.returns: Returns the date corresponding to the number of days passed since year zero. `Date32`
fromDaysSinceYearZero32.example:
SELECT
fromDaysSinceYearZero32(739136) AS date1,
fromDaysSinceYearZero32(toDaysSinceYearZero(toDate('2023-09-08'))) AS date2

fromModifiedJulianDay.description: Converts a Modified Julian Day number to a Proleptic Gregorian calendar date in text form `YYYY-MM-DD`. This function supports day number from `-678941` to `2973483` (which represent 0000-01-01 and 9999-12-31 respectively). It raises an exception if the day number is outside of the supported range.

args.name: day
args.description: Modified Julian Day number. `(U)Int*`

fromModifiedJulianDayOrNull.description: Similar to `fromModifiedJulianDay()`, but instead of raising exceptions it returns `NULL`.

args.name: day
args.description: Modified Julian Day number. `(U)Int*`

fromModifiedJulianDayOrNull.returns: Returns date in text form for valid `day` argument, otherwise `null`. `Nullable(String)`
fromModifiedJulianDayOrNull.example:
SELECT fromModifiedJulianDayOrNull(58849);
SELECT fromModifiedJulianDayOrNull(60000000); -- invalid argument, returns NULL

fromUTCTimestamp.description: Converts a date or date with time value from UTC timezone to a date or date with time value with the specified time zone. This function is mainly included for compatibility with Apache Spark and similar frameworks.

args.name: datetime
args.description: A date or date with time const value or an expression. `DateTime` or `DateTime64`

args.name: time_zone
args.description: A String type const value or an expression representing the time zone. `String`

fromUTCTimestamp.returns: Returns DateTime/DateTime64 in the specified timezone. `DateTime` or `DateTime64`

fromUnixTimestamp.description: This function converts a Unix timestamp to a calendar date and a time of a day.

args.name: timestamp
args.description: Unix timestamp or date/date with time value. `(U)Int*` or `Date` or `Date32` or `DateTime` or `DateTime64`

args.name: format
args.description: Optional. Constant format string for output formatting. `String`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Constant time zone string. `String`

fromUnixTimestamp.returns: Returns `DateTime` of the timestamp when called with one argument, or a String when called with two or three arguments. `DateTime` or `String`

fromUnixTimestamp64Micro.description: Converts a Unix timestamp in microseconds to a `DateTime64` value with microsecond precision.

args.name: value
args.description: Unix timestamp in microseconds. `Int64`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Timezone for the returned value. `String`

fromUnixTimestamp64Micro.returns: Returns a `DateTime64` value with microsecond precision. `DateTime64(6)`

fromUnixTimestamp64Milli.description: Converts a Unix timestamp in milliseconds to a `DateTime64` value with millisecond precision.

args.name: value
args.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds. `Int64`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Timezone for the returned value. `String`

fromUnixTimestamp64Nano.description: Converts a Unix timestamp in nanoseconds to a `DateTime64` value with nanosecond precision.

args.name: value
args.description: Unix timestamp in nanoseconds. `Int64`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Timezone for the returned value. `String`

fromUnixTimestamp64Nano.returns: Returns a `DateTime64` value with nanosecond precision. `DateTime64(9)`

fromUnixTimestamp64Second.description: Converts a Unix timestamp in seconds to a `DateTime64` value with second precision.

args.name: value
args.description: Unix timestamp in seconds. `Int64`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Timezone for the returned value. `String`

fromUnixTimestamp64Second.returns: Returns a `DateTime64` value with second precision. `DateTime64(0)`

fromUnixTimestampInJodaSyntax.description: This function converts a Unix timestamp to a calendar date and a time of a day.

args.name: timestamp
args.description: Unix timestamp or date/time value. `(U)Int*` or `Date` or `Date32` or `DateTime` or `DateTime64`

args.name: format
args.description: Optional. Constant format string using Joda syntax for output formatting. `String`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Constant time zone string. `String`

fromUnixTimestampInJodaSyntax.returns: Returns a date with time when called with one argument, or a String when called with two or three arguments.} `DateTime` or `String`

fuzzBits.description: Flips the bits of the input string `s`, with probability `p` for each bit.

args.name: s
args.description: String or FixedString to perform bit fuzzing on `String` or `FixedString`

args.name: p
args.description: Probability of flipping each bit as a number between `0.0` and `1.0` `Float*`

fuzzBits.returns: Returns a Fuzzed string with same type as `s`. `String` or `FixedString`

fuzzQuery.description: Parses the given query string and applies random AST mutations (fuzzing) to it. Returns the fuzzed query as a string. Non-deterministic: each call may produce a different result. Requires `allow_fuzz_query_functions = 1`.

args.name: query
args.description: The SQL query to be fuzzed. String

gccMurmurHash.description: Computes the 64-bit MurmurHash2 hash of the input value using the same seed as used by GCC.

args.name: arg1[, arg2, ...]
args.description: A variable number of arguments for which to compute the hash. `Any`

gccMurmurHash.returns: Returns the calculated hash value of the input arguments. `UInt64`
gccMurmurHash.example:
SELECT
    gccMurmurHash(1, 2, 3) AS res1,
    gccMurmurHash(('a', [1, 2, 3], 4, (4, ['foo', 'bar'], 1, (1, 2)))) AS res2

gcd.description: Returns the greatest common divisor of two values a and b.

args.name: x
args.description: First integer - `y` — Second integer

gcd.returns: The greatest common divisor of `x` and `y`.

generateRandomStructure.description: Generates random table structure in the format `column1_name column1_type, column2_name column2_type, ...`.

args.name: number_of_columns
args.description: The desired number of columns in the resultant table structure. If set to 0 or `Null`, the number of columns will be random from 1 to 128. Default value: `Null`. `UInt64`

args.name: seed
args.description: Random seed to produce stable results. If seed is not specified or set to `Null`, it is randomly generated. `UInt64`

generateSerialID.description: Generates and returns sequential numbers starting from the previous counter value. This function takes a string argument - a series identifier, and an optional starting value. The server should be configured with Keeper. The series are stored in Keeper nodes under the path, which can be configured in `series_keeper_path` in the server configuration.

args.name: series_identifier
args.description: Series identifier `const String`

args.name: start_value
args.description: Optional. Starting value for the counter. Defaults to 0. Note: this value is only used when creating a new series and is ignored if the series already exists `UInt*`

generateSerialID.returns: Returns sequential numbers starting from the previous counter value. `UInt64`

args.name: expr
args.description: An arbitrary expression used to bypass common subexpression elimination if the function is called multiple times in a query. The value of the expression has no effect on the returned Snowflake ID. Opt

generateULID.description: Generates a Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier (ULID).

args.name: x
args.description: Optional. An expression resulting in any of the supported data types. The resulting value is discarded, but the expression itself if used for bypassing common subexpression elimination if the function

args.name: expr
args.description: Optional. An arbitrary expression used to bypass common subexpression elimination if the function is called multiple times in a query. The value of the expression has no effect on the returned UUID.

args.name: expr
args.description: Optional. An arbitrary expression used to bypass common subexpression elimination if the function is called multiple times in a query. The value of the expression has no effect on the returned UUID. `

geoDistance.description: Similar to the `greatCircleDistance` function but it calculates the distance on the WGS-84 ellipsoid, which is a more accurate representation of Earth's shape than a perfect sphere. It offers the same performance as for `greatCircleDistance` and it is therefore recommended to use `geoDistance` to calculate distances on Earth.

args.name: lon1Deg
args.description: Longitude of the first point in degrees. Range: `[-180°, 180°]`. `(U)Int*` or `Float*` or `Decimal`

args.name: lat1Deg
args.description: Latitude of the first point in degrees. Range: `[-90°, 90°]`. `(U)Int*` or `Float*` or `Decimal`

args.name: lon2Deg
args.description: Longitude of the second point in degrees. Range: `[-180°, 180°]`. `(U)Int*` or `Float*` or `Decimal`

args.name: lat2Deg
args.description: Latitude of the second point in degrees. Range: `[-90°, 90°]`. `(U)Int*` or `Float*` or `Decimal`

geoDistance.returns: Returns the distance between two points on the Earth's surface, in meters `Float64`

geoToH3.description: Returns H3 point index for the given latitude, longitude, and resolution.

args.name: lat
args.description: Latitude in degrees. `Float64`

args.name: lon
args.description: Longitude in degrees. `Float64`

args.name: resolution
args.description: Index resolution with range `[0, 15]`. `UInt8`

geoToH3.returns: Returns the H3 index number, or `0` in case of error. `UInt64`

geoToMGRS.description: Encodes WGS84 geographic coordinates (longitude, latitude) as a Military Grid Reference System (MGRS) string.

args.name: longitude
args.description: Longitude in degrees. Range: `[-180°, 180°]`. `Float32` or `Float64`

args.name: latitude
args.description: Latitude in degrees. Range: `[-80°, 84°]`. `Float32` or `Float64`

args.name: precision
args.description: Optional. Number of digits for each of easting and northing. Default: 5. Range: `[0, 5]`. `(U)Int*`

geoToS2.description: Returns the S2 point index corresponding to the provided coordinates (longitude, latitude). An S2 point index is a number that internally encodes a point on the surface of a unit sphere, unlike traditional (longitude, latitude) pairs. Use `s2ToGeo` to get the coordinates from an S2 point index.

args.name: lon
args.description: Longitude. `Float64`

args.name: lat
args.description: Latitude. `Float64`

geoToUTM.description: Converts WGS84 geographic coordinates (longitude, latitude) to Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) coordinates.

args.name: longitude
args.description: Longitude in degrees. Range: `[-180°, 180°]`. `Float32` or `Float64`

args.name: latitude
args.description: Latitude in degrees. Range: `[-80°, 84°]`. `Float32` or `Float64`

args.name: zone
args.description: Optional. Force projection into this UTM zone instead of selecting it automatically. Range: `[1, 60]`. `(U)Int*`

geoToUTM.returns: Returns a named tuple `(easting, northing, zone, band)`: easting and northing in metres, the UTM zone number, and the MGRS latitude band letter (band `>= 'N'` is the northern hemisphere). `Tuple(Float64, Float64, UInt8, FixedString(1))`

geohashDecode.description: Decodes any geohash-encoded string into longitude and latitude coordinates.

args.name: hash_str
args.description: Geohash-encoded string to decode. `String` or `FixedString`

geohashDecode.returns: Returns a tuple of `(longitude, latitude)` with `Float64` precision. `Tuple(Float64, Float64)`

geohashEncode.description: Encodes longitude and latitude as a geohash-string.

args.name: longitude
args.description: Longitude part of the coordinate to encode. Range: `[-180°, 180°]`. `Float32` or `Float64`

args.name: latitude
args.description: Latitude part of the coordinate to encode. Range: `[-90°, 90°]`. `Float32` or `Float64`

args.name: precision
args.description: Optional. Length of the resulting encoded string. Default: 12. Range: `[1, 12]`. `(U)Int*`

geohashEncode.returns: Returns an alphanumeric string of the encoded coordinate (modified version of the base32-encoding alphabet is used) `String`

geohashesInBox.description: Returns an array of geohash-encoded strings of given precision that fall inside and intersect boundaries of given box, essentially a 2D grid flattened into an array.

args.name: longitude_min
args.description: Minimum longitude. Range: `[-180°, 180°]`. `Float32` or `Float64`

args.name: latitude_min
args.description: Minimum latitude. Range: `[-90°, 90°]`. `Float32` or `Float64`

args.name: longitude_max
args.description: Maximum longitude. Range: `[-180°, 180°]`. `Float32` or `Float64`

args.name: latitude_max
args.description: Maximum latitude. Range: `[-90°, 90°]`. `Float32` or `Float64`

args.name: precision
args.description: Geohash precision. Range: `[1, 12]`. `UInt8`

geohashesInBox.returns: Returns an array of precision-long strings of geohash-boxes covering the provided area, or an empty array if the minimum longitude and latitude values aren't less than the corresponding maximum values. `Array(String)`

geometryIntersectCartesian.description: Returns true if two geometries intersect (share any common point, line or area).  Unlike `polygonsIntersectCartesian`, it accepts any geometry data type  (`Point`, `LineString`,  `MultiLineString`, `Ring`,  `Polygon`, `MultiPolygon`),  including the common `Geometry` type, and the two arguments may be of different types.  Coordinates are interpreted in the Cartesian plane.

args.name: geometry1
args.description: A value of any geometry data type or `Geometry`. - `geometry2` — A value of any geometry data type or `Geometry`.

geometryIntersectCartesian.returns: Returns true (1) if the two geometries intersect. `Bool`.

geometryIntersectSpherical.description: Returns true if two geometries intersect (share any common point, line or area).  Unlike `polygonsIntersectSpherical`, it accepts any geometry data type  (`Point`, `LineString`,  `MultiLineString`, `Ring`,  `Polygon`, `MultiPolygon`),  including the common `Geometry` type, and the two arguments may be of different types.  Coordinates are interpreted as being on an ideal sphere.

args.name: geometry1
args.description: A value of any geometry data type or `Geometry`. - `geometry2` — A value of any geometry data type or `Geometry`.

geometryIntersectSpherical.returns: Returns true (1) if the two geometries intersect. `Bool`.

getClientHTTPHeader.description: Gets the value of an HTTP header. If there is no such header or the current request is not performed via the HTTP interface, the function returns an empty string. Certain HTTP headers (e.g., `Authorization`, `Authentication` and `X-ClickHouse-*`) are restricted.

args.name: name
args.description: The HTTP header name. `String`

getClientHTTPHeader.returns: Returns the value of the header. `String`
getClientHTTPHeader.example:
-- Over a non-HTTP interface (such as `clickhouse-client` or `clickhouse-local`) there are
-- no request headers, so the function returns an empty string. See the description above
-- for an HTTP example that returns the actual header value.
SELECT getClientHTTPHeader('Content-Type') SETTINGS allow_get_client_http_header = 1

getMaxTableNameLengthForDatabase.description: Returns the maximum table name length in a specified database.

args.description: The name of the specified database. `String`

getMaxTableNameLengthForDatabase.returns: Returns the length of the maximum table name, an Integer

getMergeTreeSetting.description: Returns the current value of a MergeTree setting.

args.name: setting_name
args.description: The setting name. `String`

getMergeTreeSetting.returns: Returns the merge tree setting's current value.

getOSKernelVersion.description: Returns a string with the OS kernel version.
getOSKernelVersion.returns: Returns the current OS kernel version. `String`

getServerPort.description: Returns the server's port number for a given protocol.

args.name: port_name
args.description: The name of the port. `String`

getServerSetting.description: Returns the currently set value, given a server setting name.

args.name: setting_name
args.description: The server setting name. `String`

getServerSetting.returns: Returns the server setting's current value. `Any`

getSetting.description: Returns the current value of a setting.

getSizeOfEnumType.description: Returns the number of fields in the given `Enum`.

args.name: limit

mapPopulateSeries.description: Fills missing key-value pairs in a map with integer keys. To support extending the keys beyond the largest value, a maximum key can be specified. More specifically, the function returns a map in which the keys form a series from the smallest to the largest key (or max argument if specified) with step size of 1, and corresponding values. If no value is specified for a key, a default value is use…

materialize.description: Turns a constant into a full column containing a single value. Full columns and constants are represented differently in memory. minus.description: Calculates the difference of two values `a` and `b`. The result is always signed. Similar to plus, it is possible to subtract an integer from a date or date with time. Additionally, subtraction between date with time is supported, resulting in the time difference between them.

args.name: x
args.description: Minuend. - `y` — Subtrahend.

modulo.description: Calculates the remainder of the division of two values a by b.

args.name: a
args.description: The dividend - `b` — The divisor (modulus)

moduloLegacy.description: Calculates the remainder of a division. This is the legacy modulo implementation that uses the C++ `%` operator, which may produce negative results for negative arguments. This function exists for backward compatibility with old table partitioning logic. Use `modulo` or `positiveModulo` for standard behavior.

args.name: a
args.description: The dividend. `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

args.name: b
args.description: The divisor. `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

moduloLegacy.returns: Returns the remainder of the division. `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

moduloOrNull.description: Calculates the remainder when dividing `a` by `b`. Similar to function `modulo` except that `moduloOrNull` returns `NULL` when the operation would otherwise raise a floating-point exception. For floating-point arguments this happens only when the divisor is `0`; for integer arguments it additionally covers the minimal negative value modulo `-1` (e.g. `-128 % -1` for `Int8`).

args.name: x
args.description: The dividend. `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

args.name: y
args.description: The divisor (modulus). `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

moduloOrNull.returns: Returns the remainder of the division of `x` by `y`, or `NULL` when the operation would raise a floating-point exception: when the divisor is zero, or, for integer arguments, when computing the minimal negative value modulo `-1`.

moduloOrZero.description: Like modulo but returns zero when the divisor is zero, as opposed to an exception with the modulo function.

args.name: a
args.description: The dividend. `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

args.name: b
args.description: The divisor (modulus). `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

moduloOrZero.returns: Returns the remainder of a % b, or `0` when the divisor is `0`.

args.description: Optional. Timezone name for the returned value. `String`

now.returns: Returns the current date and time. `DateTime`

now64.description: Returns the current date and time with sub-second precision at the moment of query analysis. The function is a constant expression.

args.name: scale
args.description: Optional. Tick size (precision): 10^-precision seconds. Valid range: [0 : 9]. Typically, are used - 3 (default) (milliseconds), 6 (microseconds), 9 (nanoseconds). `UInt8`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Timezone name for the returned value. `String`

now64.returns: Returns current date and time with sub-second precision. `DateTime64`

nowInBlock.description: Returns the current date and time at the moment of processing of each block of data. In contrast to the function `now`, it is not a constant expression, and the returned value will be different in different blocks for long-running queries.

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Timezone name for the returned value. `String`

nowInBlock.returns: Returns the current date and time at the moment of processing of each block of data. `DateTime`
nowInBlock.example:
SELECT
    now(),
    nowInBlock(),
    sleep(1)
FROM numbers(3)
SETTINGS max_block_size = 1
FORMAT PrettyCompactMonoBlock

nowInBlock64.description: Returns the current date and time at the moment of processing of each block of data in milliseconds. In contrast to the function now64, it is not a constant expression, and the returned value will be different in different blocks for long-running queries.

args.name: scale
args.description: Optional. Tick size (precision): 10^-precision seconds. Valid range: [0 : 9]. Typically, are used - 3 (default) (milliseconds), 6 (microseconds), 9 (nanoseconds). `UInt8`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Timezone name for the returned value. `String`

nowInBlock64.returns: Returns the current date and time at the moment of processing of each block of data with sub-second precision. `DateTime64`
nowInBlock64.example:
SELECT
    now64(),
    nowInBlock64(),
    sleep(1)
FROM numbers(3)
SETTINGS max_block_size = 1
FORMAT PrettyCompactMonoBlock

Buckets are numbered starting from 1. For each partition, the rows are assigned to buckets in order: if the number of rows is not divisible by the number of buckets, the earlier buckets receive one more row than th…

nullIf.description: Returns `NULL` if both arguments are equal.

args.name: x
args.description: The first value. `Any`

args.name: y
args.description: The second value. `Any`

nullIf.returns: Returns `NULL` if both arguments are equal, otherwise returns the first argument. `NULL` or `Nullable(x)`

nullIn.description: Checks if the left operand is a member of the right operand set. Unlike `in`, NULL values are not skipped: NULL is compared with set elements, and NULL = NULL evaluates to true.

args.name: x
args.description: The value to check. - `set` — The set of values.

nullIn.returns: Returns 1 if x is in the set, 0 otherwise. `UInt8`

nullInIgnoreSet.description: Checks if the left operand is a member of the right operand set. Unlike `in`, NULL values are not skipped: NULL is compared with set elements, and NULL = NULL evaluates to true.  This is the IgnoreSet variant used for type analysis without creating the set.

args.name: x
args.description: The value to check. - `set` — The set of values.

nullInIgnoreSet.returns: Returns 1 if x is in the set, 0 otherwise. `UInt8`

numericIndexedVectorPointwiseAdd.description: Performs pointwise addition between a numericIndexedVector and either another numericIndexedVector or a numeric constant.

args.name: v1
args.description: `numericIndexedVector`

args.name: v2
args.description: A numeric constant or numericIndexedVector object. `(U)Int*` or `Float*` or `numericIndexedVector`

numericIndexedVectorPointwiseAdd.example:
WITH
    numericIndexedVectorBuild(mapFromArrays([1, 2, 3], arrayMap(x -> toInt32(x), [10, 20, 30]))) AS vec1,
    numericIndexedVectorBuild(mapFromArrays([2, 3, 4], arrayMap(x -> toInt32(x), [10, 20, 30]))) AS vec2
SELECT
    numericIndexedVectorToMap(numericIndexedVectorPointwiseAdd(vec1, vec2)) AS res1,
    numericIndexedVectorToMap(numericIndexedVectorPointwiseAdd(vec1, 2)) AS res2;

round.description: Rounds a value to a specified number of decimal places `N`.

args.description: A number to round. `(U)Int*` or `Decimal*` or `Float*`

sum.description: Calculates the sum of numeric values.

args.name: num
args.description: Column of numeric values. `(U)Int*` or `Float*` or `Decimal*`

sum.returns: Returns the sum of the values. `(U)Int*` or `Float*` or `Decimal*`

sumCount.description: Calculates the sum of the numbers and counts the number of rows at the same time. The function is used by ClickHouse query optimizer: if there are multiple `sum`, `count` or `avg` functions in a query, they can be replaced to single `sumCount` function to reuse the calculations. The function is rarely needed to use explicitly.

args.name: x
args.description: Input value. `(U)Int*` or `Float` or `Decimal`

sumCount.returns: Returns a tuple `(sum, count)`, where `sum` is the sum of numbers and `count` is the number of rows with not-NULL values. `Tuple`

sumKahan.description: Calculates the sum of the numbers with Kahan compensated summation algorithm. Slower than `sum` function. The compensation works only for Float types.

args.name: x
args.description: Input value. `Integer` or `Float` or `Decimal`

sumKahan.returns: Returns the sum of numbers. `(U)Int*` or `Float*` or `Decimal`

sumMapFiltered.description: Like sumMap, but sums the values only for the keys that are present in a given whitelist of keys.

sumMapFilteredWithOverflow.description: Like sumMapFiltered, but performs the summation without checking for numeric overflow (the result keeps the argument's value type).

sumMapWithOverflow.description: Totals a `value` array according to the keys specified in the `key` array. Returns a tuple of two arrays: keys in sorted order, and values summed for the corresponding keys. It differs from the `sumMap` function in that it does summation with overflow - i.e. returns the same data type for the summation as the argument data type.

args.name: key
args.description: Array of keys. `Array`

args.name: value
args.description: Array of values. `Array`

sumMapWithOverflow.returns: Returns a tuple of two arrays: keys in sorted order, and values summed for the corresponding keys. `Tuple(Array, Array)`

sumMappedArrays.description: Totals one or more `value` arrays according to the keys specified in the `key` array. Returns a tuple of arrays: keys in sorted order, followed by values summed for the corresponding keys without overflow.

args.name: key
args.description: Array of keys. `Array`

args.name: value1, value2, ...
args.description: Arrays of values to sum for each key. `Array`

sumMappedArrays.returns: Returns a tuple of arrays: the first array contains keys in sorted order, followed by arrays containing values summed for the corresponding keys. `Tuple`

sumWithOverflow.description: Computes a sum of numeric values, using the same data type for the result as for the input parameters. If the sum exceeds the maximum value for this data type, it is calculated with overflow.

args.name: num
args.description: Column of numeric values. `(U)Int*` or `Float*` or `Decimal*`

sumWithOverflow.returns: The sum of the values. `(U)Int*` or `Float*` or `Decimal*`
sumWithOverflow.example:
CREATE TABLE employees
(
    id UInt32,
    name String,
    monthly_salary UInt16 -- selected so that the sum of values produces an overflow
)
ENGINE = Memory;

INSERT INTO employees VALUES
    (1, 'John', 20000),
    (2, 'Jane', 18000),
    (3, 'Bob', 12000),
    (4, 'Alice', 10000),
    (5, 'Charlie', 8000);


SELECT
    sum(monthly_salary) AS no_overflow,
    sumWithOverflow(monthly_salary) AS overflow,
    toTypeName(no_overflow),
    toTypeName(overflow)
FROM employees;

timeSeriesCopyTag.description: Copies a specified tag from one group of tags (`src_group`) to another (`dest_group`). The function replaces any previous values of the copied tag in `dest_group`. If the copied tag is not present in `src_group`, then the function will remove it from `dest_group` as well. The function mimics the copying logic of the prometheus group left/group right modifiers.

args.name: dest_group
args.description: The destination group of tags. `UInt64`

args.name: src_group
args.description: The source group of tags. `UInt64`

args.name: tag_to_copy
args.description: The name of a tag to copy. `String`

timeSeriesCopyTag.returns: Returns a group of tags containing the tags from `dest_group` along with the copied tags from `src_group`. `UInt64`
timeSeriesCopyTag.example:
SELECT timeSeriesTagsToGroup([('region', 'eu'), ('env', 'dev')], '__name__', 'http_requests_count') AS dest_group,
       timeSeriesTagsToGroup([('code', '404'), ('message', 'Page not found')], '__name__', 'http_codes') AS src_group,
       timeSeriesCopyTag(dest_group, src_group, '__name__') AS result_group,
       timeSeriesGroupToTags(result_group)

timeSeriesCopyTags.description: Copies specified tags from one group of tags (`src_group`) to another (`dest_group`). The function replaces any previous values of the copied tags in `dest_group`. If some of the copied tags don't present in `src_group` then the function will remove them in `dest_group` as well. The function mimics the copying logic of the prometheus group left/group right modifiers.

args.name: dest_group
args.description: The destination group of tags. `UInt64`

args.name: src_group
args.description: The source group of tags. `UInt64`

args.name: tags_to_copy
args.description: The names of tags to copy. `Array(String)`

args.description: Value of the time series corresponding to the timestamp. `(U)Int*` or `Float*` or `Decimal`

SET allow_experimental_time_series_aggregate_functions = 1;

    [110, 120, 130, 140, 140, 100]::Array(UInt32) AS timestamps,
    [1, 6, 8, 17, 19, 5]::Array(Float32) AS values
SELECT timeSeriesGroupArray(timestamp, value)
FROM
(
    SELECT
        arrayJoin(arrayZip(timestamps, values)) AS ts_and_val,
        ts_and_val.1 AS timestamp,
        ts_and_val.2 AS value
);

args.description: Value of the time series corresponding to the timestamp. Can be individual values or arrays. `Float*` or `Array(Float*)`

timeSeriesInstantRateToGrid.returns: Returns irate values on the specified grid. The returned array contains one value for each time grid point. The value is NULL if there are not enough samples within the window to calculate the instant rate value for a particular grid point. `Array(Nullable(Float64))`

timeSeriesJoinTags.description: Joins the values of specified tags extracted from a group of tags. The function inserts a separator between joined values and returns a new group of tags with the tag `dest_tag` set to the joined value. This function mimics the logic of the prometheus function label_join().

args.name: group
args.description: A group of tags. `UInt64`

args.name: dest_tag
args.description: The name of a tag with the joined result which will be added to the `group`. `String`

args.name: separator
args.description: A separator to insert between joined values. `String`

args.name: src_tags
args.description: The names of source tags with values which will be joined. `Array(String)`

timeSeriesJoinTags.returns: Returns a new group of tags with the `dest_tag` tag set to the joined result. `UInt64`
timeSeriesJoinTags.example:
SELECT timeSeriesTagsToGroup([('__name__', 'up'), ('job', 'api-server'), ('src1', 'a'), ('src2', 'b'), ('src3', 'c')]) AS group,
       timeSeriesJoinTags(group, 'foo', ',', ['src1', 'src2', 'src3']) AS result_group,
       timeSeriesGroupToTags(result_group)

timeSeriesLastTwoSamples.description: Aggregate function for re-sampling time series data for PromQL-like irate and idelta calculation.

args.name: timestamp
args.description: Timestamp of the sample. `DateTime` or `DateTime64` or `(U)Int*` or `Int*`

args.name: value
args.description: Value of the time series corresponding to the timestamp. `Float32` or `Float64`

timeSeriesLastTwoSamples.returns: Returns a pair of arrays of equal length from 0 to 2. The first array contains the timestamps of sampled time series, the second array contains the corresponding values of the time series. `Tuple(Array(DateTime), Array(Float64))`

timeSeriesPredictLinearToGrid.description: Aggregate function that takes time series data as pairs of timestamps and values and calculates a PromQL-like linear prediction with a specified prediction timestamp offset from this data on a regular time grid described by start timestamp, end timestamp and step. For each point on the grid the samples for calculating `predict_linear` are considered within the specified time window.

args.name: timestamp
args.description: Timestamp of the sample. Can be individual values or arrays. - `value` — Value of the time series corresponding to the timestamp. Can be individual values or arrays.

timeSeriesPredictLinearToGrid.returns: `predict_linear` values on the specified grid as an `Array(Nullable(Float64))`. The returned array contains one value for each time grid point. The value is NULL if there are not enough samples within the window to calculate the rate value for a particular grid point.

timeSeriesRange.description: Generates a range of timestamps [start_timestamp, start_timestamp + step, start_timestamp + 2 * step, ..., end_timestamp].

args.name: start_timestamp
args.description: Start of the range. `DateTime64` or `DateTime` or `UInt32`

args.name: end_timestamp
args.description: End of the range. `DateTime64` or `DateTime` or `UInt32`

args.name: step
args.description: Step of the range in seconds `UInt32/64` or `Decimal32/64`

timeSeriesRateToGrid.description: Aggregate function that takes time series data as pairs of timestamps and values and calculates PromQL-like rate from this data on a regular time grid described by start timestamp, end timestamp and step. For each point on the grid the samples for calculating `rate` are considered within the specified time window.

args.name: timestamp
args.description: Timestamp of the sample. Can be individual values or arrays. `UInt32` or `DateTime` or `Array(UInt32)` or `Array(DateTime)`

args.name: value
args.description: Value of the time series corresponding to the timestamp. Can be individual values or arrays. `Float*` or `Array(Float*)`

timeSeriesRateToGrid.returns: Returns rate values on the specified grid. The returned array contains one value for each time grid point. The value is NULL if there are not enough samples within the window to calculate the rate value for a particular grid point. `Array(Nullable(Float64))`

timeSeriesRemoveAllTagsExcept.description: Removes all tags except specified ones from a group of tags. See also function timeSeriesRemoveTag(), timeSeriesRemoveTags().

args.name: group
args.description: A group of tags. `UInt64`

args.name: tags_to_keep
args.description: The names of tags to keep in the group. `Array(String)`

timeSeriesRemoveAllTagsExcept.returns: A new group of tags with only the specified tags kept. `UInt64`
timeSeriesRemoveAllTagsExcept.example:
SELECT timeSeriesTagsToGroup([('region', 'eu'), ('env', 'dev')], '__name__', 'http_requests_count') AS group,
       timeSeriesRemoveAllTagsExcept(group, ['env']) AS result_group,
       timeSeriesGroupToTags(result_group)

timeSeriesRemoveTag.description: Removes a specified tag from a group of tags. If there is no such tag in the group then the group is returned unchanged. See also function timeSeriesRemoveTags(), timeSeriesRemoveAllTagsExcept().

args.name: group
args.description: A group of tags. `UInt64`

args.name: tag_to_remove
args.description: The name of a tag to remove from the group. `String`

timeSeriesRemoveTag.returns: A new group of tags without the specified tag. `UInt64`
timeSeriesRemoveTag.example:
SELECT timeSeriesTagsToGroup([('region', 'eu'), ('env', 'dev')], '__name__', 'http_requests_count') AS group_of_3,
       timeSeriesRemoveTag(group_of_3, '__name__') AS group_of_2,
       timeSeriesGroupToTags(group_of_2),
       timeSeriesRemoveTag(group_of_2, 'env') AS group_of_1,
       timeSeriesGroupToTags(group_of_1),
       timeSeriesRemoveTag(group_of_1, 'region') AS empty_group,
       timeSeriesGroupToTags(empty_group)

timeSeriesRemoveTags.description: Removes specified tags from a group of tags. If some of the specified tags are not in the group of tags the function ignores them. See also function timeSeriesRemoveTag(), timeSeriesRemoveAllTagsExcept().

args.name: group
args.description: A group of tags. `UInt64`

args.name: tags_to_remove
args.description: The names of tags to remove from the group. `Array(String)`

timeSeriesRemoveTags.returns: A new group of tags without the specified tags. `UInt64`
timeSeriesRemoveTags.example:
SELECT timeSeriesTagsToGroup([('region', 'eu'), ('env', 'dev')], '__name__', 'http_requests_count') AS group_of_3,
       timeSeriesRemoveTags(group_of_3, ['env', 'region']) AS group_of_1,
       timeSeriesGroupToTags(group_of_1),
       timeSeriesRemoveTags(group_of_1, ['__name__', 'nonexistent']) AS empty_group,
       timeSeriesGroupToTags(empty_group)

timeSeriesReplaceTag.description: Matches the regular expression `regex` against the value of the tag `src_tag`. If it matches, the value of the tag `dest_tag` in the returned group will be the expansion of `replacement`, together with the original tags in the input. This function mimics the logic of the prometheus function label_replace().

args.name: group
args.description: A group of tags. `UInt64`

args.name: dest_tag
args.description: The name of a destination tag to get the result group. `String`

args.name: replacement
args.description: A replacement pattern, can contain $1, $2 or $name to refer capturing groups in the regular expression 'regex'. `String`

args.name: src_tag
args.description: The name of a tag which value is used to match the regular expression 'regex'. `String`

args.name: regex
args.description: A regular expression. `String`

timeSeriesReplaceTag.returns: A new group of tags with maybe `dest_tag` added. `UInt64`
timeSeriesReplaceTag.example:
SELECT timeSeriesTagsToGroup([('__name__', 'up'), ('job', 'api-server'), ('service', 'a:c')]) AS group,
       timeSeriesReplaceTag(group, 'foo', '$1', 'service', '(.*):.*') AS result_group,
       timeSeriesGroupToTags(result_group)

timeSeriesResampleToGridWithStaleness.description: Aggregate function that takes time series data as pairs of timestamps and values and re-samples this data to a regular time grid described by start timestamp, end timestamp and step. For each point on the grid the most recent (within the specified time window) sample is chosen.

args.name: timestamp
args.description: Timestamp of the sample. Can be individual values or arrays. `UInt32` or `DateTime` or `Array(UInt32)` or `Array(DateTime)`

args.name: value
args.description: Value of the time series corresponding to the timestamp. Can be individual values or arrays. `Float*` or `Array(Float*)`

timeSeriesResampleToGridWithStaleness.returns: Returns time series values re-sampled to the specified grid. The returned array contains one value for each time grid point. The value is NULL if there is no sample for a particular grid point. `Array(Nullable(Float64))`

timeSeriesResetsToGrid.description: Aggregate function that takes time series data as pairs of timestamps and values and calculates PromQL-like resets from this data on a regular time grid described by start timestamp, end timestamp and step. For each point on the grid the samples for calculating `resets` are considered within the specified time window.

args.name: timestamp
args.description: Timestamp of the sample. Can be individual values or arrays. - `value` — Value of the time series corresponding to the timestamp. Can be individual values or arrays.

timeSeriesResetsToGrid.returns: `resets` values on the specified grid as an `Array(Nullable(Float64))`. The returned array contains one value for each time grid point. The value is NULL if there are no samples within the window to calculate the resets value for a particular grid point.

timeSeriesStoreTags.description: Stores in the query context a mapping between a specified identifier of a time series and a set of tags. Functions timeSeriesIdToTags() and timeSeriesIdToGroup() can be used to access this mapping later during the query execution.

args.name: id
args.description: Identifier of a time series. `UInt64` or `UInt128` or `UUID` or `FixedString(16)`

args.name: tags_array
args.description: Array of pairs (tag_name, tag_value). `Array(Tuple(String, String))` or `NULL`

args.name: separate_tag_name_i
args.description: The name of a tag. `String` or `FixedString`

args.name: separate_tag_value_i
args.description: The value of a tag. `String` or `FixedString` or `Nullable(String)`

timeSeriesStoreTags.returns: Returns the identifier of a time series (i.e. just the first argument).
timeSeriesStoreTags.example:
SELECT 8374283493092 AS id,
       timeSeriesStoreTags(id, [('region', 'eu'), ('env', 'dev')], '__name__', 'http_requests_count') AS same_id,
       throwIf(same_id != id),
       timeSeriesIdToTags(same_id),
       timeSeriesGroupToTags(timeSeriesIdToGroup(same_id))

timeSeriesTagsToGroup.description: Returns a group of tags associated with specified tags. If the same group of tags is found multiple times during the query execution, the function returns the same group. For an empty set of tags the function always returns 0. See also function timeSeriesGroupToTags().

args.name: tags_array
args.description: Array of pairs (tag_name, tag_value). `Array(Tuple(String, String))` or `NULL`

args.name: tag_name_i
args.description: The name of a tag. `String` or `FixedString`

args.name: tag_value_i
args.description: The value of a tag. `String` or `FixedString` or `Nullable(String)`

timeSeriesTagsToGroup.returns: Returns a group of tags associated with the specified tags. `UInt64`
timeSeriesTagsToGroup.example:
SELECT timeSeriesTagsToGroup([('region', 'eu'), ('env', 'dev')], '__name__', 'http_requests_count') AS group1,
       timeSeriesTagsToGroup([], '__name__', 'http_failures') AS group2,
       timeSeriesTagsToGroup([]) AS empty_group,
       timeSeriesTagsToGroup([], '__name__', 'http_failures') AS same_group2,
       throwIf(same_group2 != group2),
       timeSeriesGroupToTags(group2)

timeSeriesThrowDuplicateSeriesIf.description: Checks the `condition` and if it's true throws an exception with the following message `Multiple series have the same tags <tags>, duplicate series in the same result set are not allowed`. If the `condition` is false the function returns `0`. This function is similar to throwIf(), but uses a different error code and formats the error message differently.

args.name: condition
args.description: Condition to check, usually contains function count() `UInt8`

args.name: group
args.description: Group of tags. `UInt64`

timeSlot.description: Round the time to the start of a half-an-hour length interval.

args.name: time
args.description: Time to round to the start of a half-an-hour length interval. `DateTime` or `Date32` or `DateTime64`

args.name: time_zone
args.description: Optional. A String type const value or an expression representing the time zone. `String`

timeSlot.returns: Returns the time rounded to the start of a half-an-hour length interval. `DateTime`

timeSlots.description: For a time interval starting at `StartTime` and continuing for `Duration` seconds, it returns an array of moments in time, consisting of points from this interval rounded down to the `Size` in seconds. `Size` is an optional parameter set to 1800 (30 minutes) by default.

args.name: StartTime
args.description: Starting time for the interval. `DateTime` or `DateTime64`

args.name: Duration
args.description: Duration of the interval in seconds. `UInt32` or `DateTime64`

args.name: Size
args.description: Optional. Size of time slots in seconds. Default is 1800 (30 minutes). `UInt32` or `DateTime64`

timeSlots.returns: Returns an array of DateTime/DateTime64 (return type matches the type of `StartTime`). For DateTime64, the return value's scale can differ from the scale of `StartTime` - the highest scale among all given arguments is taken. `Array(DateTime)` or `Array(DateTime64)`

timestamp.description: Converts the first argument `expr` to type `DateTime64(6)`. If a second argument `expr_time` is provided, it adds the specified time to the converted value.

args.name: expr
args.description: Date or date with time. `String`

args.name: expr_time
args.description: Optional. Time to add to the converted value. `String`

timestamp.returns: Returns the converted value of `expr`, or `expr` with added time `DateTime64(6)`

timezone.description: Returns the time zone name of the current session or converts a time zone offset or name to a canonical time zone name.
timezone.returns: Returns the canonical time zone name as a `String`

timezoneOf.description: Returns the timezone name of a `DateTime` or `DateTime64` value.

args.name: datetime
args.description: A value of type. `DateTime` or `DateTime64`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Timezone name to convert the `datetime` value's timezone to. `String`

timezoneOffset.description: Returns the timezone offset in seconds from UTC. The function takes daylight saving time and historical timezone changes at the specified date and time into account.

args.name: datetime
args.description: `DateTime` value to get the timezone offset for. `DateTime` or `DateTime64`

timezoneOffset.returns: Returns the offset from UTC in seconds `Int32`
timezoneOffset.example:
SELECT toDateTime('2021-04-21 10:20:30', 'America/New_York') AS Time,
toTypeName(Time) AS Type,
timezoneOffset(Time) AS Offset_in_seconds,
(Offset_in_seconds / 3600) AS Offset_in_hours;

toBFloat16.description: Converts an input value to a value of type BFloat16. Throws an exception in case of an error.

args.name: expr
args.description: Expression returning a number or a string representation of a number. `Expression`

toBFloat16.example:
SELECT
toBFloat16(toFloat32(42.7)),
toBFloat16(toFloat32('42.7')),
toBFloat16('42.7')
FORMAT Vertical;

toBFloat16OrNull.description: Converts a String input value to a value of type BFloat16. If the string does not represent a floating point value, the function returns NULL.

args.name: x
args.description: A String representation of a number. `String`

toBFloat16OrNull.returns: Reurns a 16-bit brain-float value, otherwise `NULL`. `BFloat16` or `NULL`
toBFloat16OrNull.example:
SELECT toBFloat16OrNull('0x5E'), -- unsupported arguments
       toBFloat16OrNull('12.3'), -- typical use
       toBFloat16OrNull('12.3456789') -- silent loss of precision

toBFloat16OrZero.description: Converts a String input value to a value of type BFloat16. If the string does not represent a floating point value, the function returns zero.

args.name: x
args.description: A String representation of a number. `String`

toBFloat16OrZero.example:
SELECT toBFloat16OrZero('0x5E'), -- unsupported arguments
       toBFloat16OrZero('12.3'), -- typical use
       toBFloat16OrZero('12.3456789') -- silent loss of precision

toBool.description: Converts an input value to a value of type Bool.

args.name: expr
args.description: Expression returning a number or a string. For strings, accepts 'true' or 'false' (case-insensitive). `(U)Int*` or `Float*` or `String` or `Expression`

toBool.returns: Returns `true` or `false` based on evaluation of the argument. `Bool`
toBool.example:
SELECT
    toBool(toUInt8(1)),
    toBool(toInt8(-1)),
    toBool(toFloat32(1.01)),
    toBool('true'),
    toBool('false'),
    toBool('FALSE')
FORMAT Vertical

toColumnTypeName.description: Returns the internal name of the data type of the given value. Unlike function `toTypeName`, the returned data type potentially includes internal wrapper columns like `Const` and `LowCardinality`.

args.name: value
args.description: Value for which to return the internal data type. `Any`

toColumnTypeName.returns: Returns the internal data type used to represent the value. `String`

toDate.description: Converts an input value to type `Date`. Supports conversion from String, FixedString, DateTime, or numeric types.

args.name: x
args.description: Input value to convert. `String` or `FixedString` or `DateTime` or `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

toDate32.description: Converts the argument to the Date32 data type. If the value is outside the range, `toDate32` returns the border values supported by Date32. If the argument is of type `Date`, it's bounds are taken into account.

args.name: expr
args.description: The value to convert. `String` or `UInt32` or `Date`

toDate32.example:
SELECT toDate32('2025-01-01') AS value, toTypeName(value)
FORMAT Vertical

toDate32OrDefault.description: Converts the argument to the Date32 data type. If the value is outside the range, `toDate32OrDefault` returns the lower border value supported by Date32. If the argument has Date type, it's borders are taken into account. Returns default value if an invalid argument is received.

args.name: expr
args.description: Expression returning a number or a string representation of a number. `String` or `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

args.name: default
args.description: Optional. The default value to return if parsing is unsuccessful. `Date32`

toDate32OrDefault.returns: Value of type Date32 if successful, otherwise returns the default value if passed or 1900-01-01 if not. `Date32`

toDate32OrNull.description: Converts an input value to a value of type Date32 but returns `NULL` if an invalid argument is received. The same as `toDate32` but returns `NULL` if an invalid argument is received.

args.name: x
args.description: A string representation of a date. `String`

toDate32OrNull.returns: Returns a Date32 value if successful, otherwise `NULL`. `Date32` or `NULL`

toDate32OrZero.description: Converts an input value to a value of type Date32 but returns the lower boundary of Date32 if an invalid argument is received. The same as toDate32 but returns lower boundary of Date32 if an invalid argument is received.

args.name: x
args.description: A string representation of a date. `String`

toDate32OrZero.returns: Returns a Date32 value if successful, otherwise the lower boundary of Date32 (`1900-01-01`). `Date32`

toDateOrDefault.description: Like toDate but if unsuccessful, returns a default value which is either the second argument (if specified), or otherwise the lower boundary of Date.

args.name: expr
args.description: Expression returning a number or a string representation of a number. `String` or `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

args.name: default
args.description: Optional. The default value to return if parsing is unsuccessful. `Date`

toDateOrDefault.returns: Value of type Date if successful, otherwise returns the default value if passed or 1970-01-01 if not. `Date`

toDateOrNull.description: Converts an input value to a value of type `Date` but returns `NULL` if an invalid argument is received. The same as `toDate` but returns `NULL` if an invalid argument is received. An integer argument is interpreted the same way as by `toDate` (a number of days since 1970-01-01 if it does not exceed 65535, a Unix timestamp otherwise), and produces `NULL` if it is out of range of the `Date` type.

args.name: x
args.description: A string representation of a date, or an integer number of days or a Unix timestamp. `String` or `(U)Int8/16/32/64`

toDateOrNull.returns: Returns a Date value if successful, otherwise `NULL`. `Date` or `NULL`

toDateOrZero.description: Converts an input value to a value of type `Date` but returns the lower boundary of `Date` if an invalid argument is received. The same as toDate but returns lower boundary of `Date` if an invalid argument is received.

args.name: x
args.description: A string representation of a date. `String`

toDateOrZero.returns: Returns a Date value if successful, otherwise the lower boundary of Date (`1970-01-01`). `Date`

toDateTime.description: Converts an input value to type DateTime.

args.name: expr
args.description: The value. `String` or `Int` or `Date` or `DateTime`

args.name: time_zone
args.description: Time zone. `String`

DateTime32 provides extended range compared to `DateTime`, supporting dates from `1900-01-01` to `2299-12-31`.

args.name: x
args.description: Input value to convert. `String` or `FixedString` or `UInt*` or `Float*` or `Date` or `DateTime` or `DateTime64`

args.name: timezone

toDateTime64.description: Converts an input value to a value of type `DateTime64`.

args.name: expr
args.description: Expression returning a number or a string representation of a number. `Expression`

args.name: scale
args.description: Tick size (precision): 10^(-scale) seconds. `UInt8`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Time zone for the specified `DateTime64` object. `String`

toDateTime64.returns: Returns a calendar date and time of day, with sub-second precision. `DateTime64`

toDateTime64OrDefault.description: Like toDateTime64, this function converts an input value to a value of type DateTime64, but returns either the default value of DateTime64 or the provided default if an invalid argument is received.

args.description: Expression returning a number or a string representation of a number. `String` or `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

args.name: scale
args.description: Tick size (precision): 10^-precision seconds. `UInt8`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Time zone. `String`

args.name: default
args.description: Optional. The default value to return if parsing is unsuccessful. `DateTime64`

toDateTime64OrDefault.returns: Value of type DateTime64 if successful, otherwise returns the default value if passed or 1970-01-01 00:00:00.000 if not. `DateTime64`

toDateTime64OrNull.description: Converts an input value to a value of type `DateTime64` but returns `NULL` if an invalid argument is received. An integer argument is interpreted as a Unix timestamp in whole seconds and produces `NULL` if it is out of range of the `DateTime64` type.

args.name: precision

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Time zone of the returned value. `String`

toDateTime64OrNull.returns: Returns a DateTime64 value if successful, otherwise `NULL`. `DateTime64` or `NULL`

toDateTime64OrZero.description: Converts an input value to a value of type DateTime64 but returns the lower boundary of DateTime64 if an invalid argument is received. The same as toDateTime64 but returns lower boundary of DateTime64 if an invalid argument is received.

args.name: x
args.description: A string representation of a date with time and subsecond precision. `String`

toDateTime64OrZero.returns: Returns a DateTime64 value if successful, otherwise the lower boundary of DateTime64 (`1970-01-01 00:00:00.000`). `DateTime64`

toDateTimeOrDefault.description: Like toDateTime but if unsuccessful, returns a default value which is either the third argument (if specified), or otherwise the lower boundary of DateTime.

args.name: expr
args.description: Expression returning a number or a string representation of a number. `String` or `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Time zone. `String`

args.name: default
args.description: Optional. The default value to return if parsing is unsuccessful. `DateTime`

toDateTimeOrDefault.returns: Value of type DateTime if successful, otherwise returns the default value if passed or 1970-01-01 00:00:00 if not. `DateTime`

toDateTimeOrNull.description: Converts an input value to a value of type `DateTime` but returns `NULL` if an invalid argument is received. The same as `toDateTime` but returns `NULL` if an invalid argument is received. An integer argument is interpreted as a Unix timestamp and produces `NULL` if it is out of range of the `DateTime` type.

args.name: x
args.description: A string representation of a date with time, or an integer Unix timestamp. `String` or `(U)Int8/16/32/64`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Time zone of the returned value. `String`

toDateTimeOrNull.returns: Returns a `DateTime` value if successful, otherwise `NULL`. `DateTime` or `NULL`

toDateTimeOrZero.description: Converts an input value to a value of type DateTime but returns the lower boundary of DateTime if an invalid argument is received. The same as toDateTime but returns lower boundary of DateTime if an invalid argument is received.

args.name: x
args.description: A string representation of a date with time. `String`

toDateTimeOrZero.returns: Returns a DateTime value if successful, otherwise the lower boundary of DateTime (`1970-01-01 00:00:00`). `DateTime`

toDayOfYear.description: Returns the number of the day within the year (1-366) of a `Date` or `DateTime` value.

toDayOfYear.returns: Returns the day of the year of the given Date or DateTime `UInt16`

toDaysInMonth.description: Returns the number of days in the month of a `Date` or `DateTime`.

args.name: datetime
args.description: Date or date with time to get the number of days in the month from. `Date` or `Date32` or `DateTime` or `DateTime64`

toDaysInMonth.returns: Returns the number of days in the month of the given date/time. `UInt8`

toDaysSinceYearZero.description: For a given date, returns the number of days which have passed since 1 January 0000 in the proleptic Gregorian calendar defined by ISO 8601.

args.description: The date or date with time for which to calculate the number of days since year zero from. `Date` or `Date32` or `DateTime` or `DateTime64`

args.name: time_zone

toIPv4.description: Converts a string or a UInt32 form of IPv4 address to type IPv4. It is similar to `IPv4StringToNum` and `IPv4NumToString` functions but it supports both string and unsigned integer data types as input arguments.

args.name: x
args.description: An IPv4 address `String` or `UInt8/16/32`

toIPv4OrDefault.description: Converts a string or a UInt32 form of an IPv4 address to `IPv4` type. If the IPv4 address has an invalid format, it returns `0.0.0.0` (0 IPv4), or the provided IPv4 default.

args.name: string
args.description: IP address string to convert. `String`

args.name: default
args.description: Optional. The value to return if string is an invalid IPv4 address. `IPv4`

toIPv4OrDefault.returns: Returns a string converted to the current IPv4 address, or the default value if conversion fails. `IPv4`
toIPv4OrDefault.example:
WITH
    '192.168.1.1' AS valid_IPv4_string,
    '999.999.999.999' AS invalid_IPv4_string,
    'not_an_ip' AS malformed_string
SELECT
    toIPv4OrDefault(valid_IPv4_string) AS valid,
    toIPv4OrDefault(invalid_IPv4_string) AS default_value,
    toIPv4OrDefault(malformed_string, toIPv4('8.8.8.8')) AS provided_default;

toIPv4OrNull.example:
SELECT
    toIPv4OrNull('192.168.1.1') AS valid_ip,
    toIPv4OrNull('invalid.ip') AS invalid_ip

toIPv4OrZero.example:
SELECT

    toIPv4OrZero('invalid.ip') AS invalid_ip

toIPv6.description: onverts a string or a `UInt128` form of IPv6 address to `IPv6` type. For strings, if the IPv6 address has an invalid format, returns an empty value. Similar to `IPv6StringToNum` and `IPv6NumToString` functions, which convert IPv6 address to and from binary format (i.e. `FixedString(16)`).

args.name: x
args.description: An IP address. `String` or `UInt128`

toIPv6.example:
WITH '2001:438:ffff::407d:1bc1' AS IPv6_string
SELECT
    hex(IPv6StringToNum(IPv6_string)),
    hex(toIPv6(IPv6_string));

args.name: string
args.description: IP address string to convert. - `default` — Optional. The value to return if string has an invalid format.

toIPv6OrDefault.returns: Returns the IPv6 address, otherwise `::` or the provided optional default if argument `string` has an invalid format. `IPv6`
toIPv6OrDefault.example:
WITH
    '2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334' AS valid_IPv6_string,
    '2001:0db8:85a3::8a2e:370g:7334' AS invalid_IPv6_string,
    'not_an_ipv6' AS malformed_string
SELECT
    toIPv6OrDefault(valid_IPv6_string) AS valid,
    toIPv6OrDefault(invalid_IPv6_string) AS default_value,
    toIPv6OrDefault(malformed_string, toIPv6('::1')) AS provided_default;

    toIPv6OrNull('2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334') AS valid_ipv6,

args.description: Input value to convert. `String` or `FixedString` or `DateTime` or `DateTime64` or `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

toTime64.description: Converts an input value to type Time64. Supports conversion from String, FixedString, DateTime64, or numeric types representing seconds since midnight. Provides sub-second precision for time values, up to `scale` fractional digits.

args.name: x
args.description: Input value to convert. `String` or `FixedString` or `DateTime64` or `(U)Int*` or `Float*`

args.name: scale
args.description: Precision (number of fractional digits, `0`–`9`) of the resulting `Time64`. `(U)Int*`

toTime64.returns: Returns the converted value with the requested `scale`. `Time64`

toTime64OrNull.description: Converts an input value to a value of type `Time64` but returns `NULL` in case of an error. Like `toTime64` but returns `NULL` instead of throwing an exception on conversion errors.

args.name: x
args.description: A string representation of a time with subsecond precision. `String`

toTime64OrNull.returns: Returns a Time64 value if successful, otherwise `NULL`. `Time64` or `NULL`

toTime64OrZero.description: Converts an input value to a value of type Time64 but returns `00:00:00.000` in case of an error. Like `toTime64` but returns `00:00:00.000` instead of throwing an exception on conversion errors.

args.name: x
args.description: A string representation of a time with subsecond precision. `String`

toTime64OrZero.returns: Returns a Time64 value if successful, otherwise `00:00:00.000`. `Time64`

toTimeOrNull.description: Converts an input value to a value of type Time but returns `NULL` in case of an error. Like `toTime` but returns `NULL` instead of throwing an exception on conversion errors.

toTimeOrNull.returns: Returns a Time value if successful, otherwise `NULL`. `Time` or `NULL`

toTimeOrZero.description: Converts an input value to a value of type Time but returns `00:00:00` in case of an error. Like toTime but returns `00:00:00` instead of throwing an exception on conversion errors.

args.name: x
