toTimeOrZero.returns: Returns a Time value if successful, otherwise `00:00:00`. `Time`

toTimeWithFixedDate.description: Extracts the time component of a date or date with time. The returned result is an offset to a fixed point in time, currently `1970-01-02`, but the exact point in time is an implementation detail which may change in future.

args.name: date
args.description: Date to convert to a time. `Date` or `DateTime` or `DateTime64`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Timezone for the returned value. `String`

toTimeWithFixedDate.returns: Returns the time component of a date or date with time in the form of an offset to a fixed point in time (selected as 1970-01-02, currently). `DateTime`
toTimeWithFixedDate.example: SELECT toTimeWithFixedDate('2025-06-15 12:00:00'::DateTime) - toTimeWithFixedDate('2024-05-10 11:00:00'::DateTime) AS result, toTypeName(result)

toTimezone.description: Converts a `DateTime` or `DateTime64` to the specified time zone. The internal value (number of unix seconds) of the data doesn't change. Only the value's time zone attribute and the value's string representation changes.

args.name: date
args.description: The value to convert. `DateTime` or `DateTime64`

args.name: timezone
args.description: The target time zone name. `String`

toTimezone.returns: Returns the same timestamp as the input, but with the specified time zone `DateTime` or `DateTime64`
toTimezone.example:
SELECT toDateTime('2019-01-01 00:00:00', 'UTC') AS time_utc,
toTypeName(time_utc) AS type_utc,
toInt32(time_utc) AS int32utc,
toTimezone(time_utc, 'Asia/Yekaterinburg') AS time_yekat,
toTypeName(time_yekat) AS type_yekat,
toInt32(time_yekat) AS int32yekat,
toTimezone(time_utc, 'US/Samoa') AS time_samoa,
toTypeName(time_samoa) AS type_samoa,
toInt32(time_samoa) AS int32samoa
FORMAT Vertical;

toUnixTimestamp.description: Converts a `String`, `Date`, or `DateTime` to a Unix timestamp (seconds since `1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC`) as `UInt32`.

args.name: date
args.description: Value to convert. `Date` or `Date32` or `DateTime` or `DateTime64` or `String`

args.name: timezone
args.description: Optional. Timezone to use for conversion. If not specified, the server's timezone is used. `String`

toUnixTimestamp.example:
SELECT
'2017-11-05 08:07:47' AS dt_str,
toUnixTimestamp(dt_str) AS from_str,
toUnixTimestamp(dt_str, 'Asia/Tokyo') AS from_str_tokyo,
toUnixTimestamp(toDateTime(dt_str)) AS from_datetime,
toUnixTimestamp(toDateTime64(dt_str, 0)) AS from_datetime64,
toUnixTimestamp(toDate(dt_str)) AS from_date,
toUnixTimestamp(toDate32(dt_str)) AS from_date32
FORMAT Vertical;

toUnixTimestamp64Micro.example:

SELECT toUnixTimestamp64Micro(dt64);

toWeek.description: This function returns the week number for date or datetime. The two-argument form of `toWeek()` enables you to specify whether the week starts on Sunday or Monday and whether the return value should be in the range from `0` to `53` or from `1` to `53`.

args.description: Date or date with time to get the week number from. `Date` or `DateTime`

args.description: Optional. A mode `0` to `9` determines the first day of the week and the range of the week number. Default `0`. - `time_zone` — Optional. Time zone. `String`

toWeek.returns: Returns the week number according to the specified mode. `UInt32`
toWeek.example: SELECT toDate('2016-12-27') AS date, toWeek(date) AS week0, toWeek(date,1) AS week1, toWeek(date,9) AS week9

args.name: query
args.description: A ClickHouse SQL query string. String.

tokenizeQuery.returns: An array of named tuples `(begin UInt64, end UInt64, type Enum8(...))` representing the tokens of the query. `Array(Tuple(begin UInt64, end UInt64, type Enum8(...)))`

tokens.description: Splits a string into tokens using the given tokenizer.

args.name: value
args.description: The input string. `String` or `FixedString`

args.name: tokenizer
args.description: The tokenizer to use. Valid arguments are `splitByNonAlpha`, `splitByString`, `asciiCJK`, `ngrams`, `sparseGrams`, and `array`. Optional, if not set explicitly, defaults to `splitByNonAlpha`. `const S

args.name: n
args.description: Only relevant if argument `tokenizer` is `ngrams`: An optional parameter which defines the length of the ngrams. If not set explicitly, defaults to `3`. `const UInt8`

args.name: separators
args.description: Only relevant if argument `tokenizer` is `split`: An optional parameter which defines the separator strings. If not set explicitly, defaults to `[' ']`. `const Array(String)`

args.name: min_length
args.description: Only relevant if argument `tokenizer` is `sparseGrams`: An optional parameter which defines the minimum gram length, defaults to 3. `const UInt8`

args.name: max_length
args.description: Only relevant if argument `tokenizer` is `sparseGrams`: An optional parameter which defines the maximum gram length, defaults to 100. `const UInt8`

args.name: min_cutoff_length
args.description: Only relevant if argument `tokenizer` is `sparseGrams`: An optional parameter which defines the minimum cutoff length. `const UInt8`

tokens.returns: Returns the resulting array of tokens from input string. `Array`
tokens.example: SELECT tokens('test1,;\\\\ test2,;\\\\ test3,;\\\\   test4') AS tokens;

topK.description: Returns an array of the approximately most frequent values in the specified column. The resulting array is sorted in descending order of approximate frequency of values (not by the values themselves).

args.description: The name of the column for which to find the most frequent values. `String`

welchTTest.description: Applies Welch's t-test to samples from two populations.

widthBucket.description: Returns the number of the bucket in which parameter `operand` falls in a histogram having count equal-width buckets spanning the range `low` to `high`. Returns 0 if `operand` is less than `low`, and returns `count`+1 if `operand` is greater than or equal to `high`. There is also a case insensitive alias called `WIDTH_BUCKET` to provide compatibility with other databases.

args.name: operand
args.description: The value for which to determine the bucket. `(U)Int8/16/32/64`

args.name: low
args.description: The lower bound of the histogram range. `(U)Int8/16/32/64`

args.name: high
args.description: The upper bound of the histogram range. `(U)Int8/16/32/64`

args.name: count
args.description: The number of equal-width buckets. Cannot be zero. `UInt8/16/32/64`

widthBucket.returns: Returns the bucket number as an integer. Returns 0 if operand < low, returns count+1 if operand >= high. `UInt8/16/32/64`
